meal.title: Using Comparison Operators to Enforce Positive Values
meal.objective: Compare numbers and ensure a value is greater than zero

voice.script: What if your bet could be zero? How do you make sure a number is positive? These are the three operators: greater than, less than, and greater than or equal to. The greater than sign checks if the left number is larger than the right one. The less than sign checks if it is smaller. Greater than or equal to checks if it is larger or exactly the same. Here’s the code that validates the deposit amount. It asks for a number, turns it into an integer, then checks if the value is greater than zero. The program tells you whether the amount is accepted. The decision diamond shows the check, sending you to an accepted path or an error message. Remember: use the > operator to ensure a value is positive.
